title: Briefcase Full of Blues - Wikipedia
notes: The Blues Brothers' debut album (Atlantic, 28 November 1978), recorded live at the Universal Amphitheatre, Los Angeles, on 9 September 1978. Personnel (after Richard Buskin in Sound on Sound and the liner notes): Steve "Getdwa" Jordan, drums and backing vocals; Steve Cropper and Matt Murphy, guitars; Donald "Duck" Dunn, bass; Paul Shaffer, keyboards. Soul Man was a single and reached 14 in Billboard.

title: Steve Jordan (Billy Amendola, Modern Drummer, July 2005)
notes: Timpani and orchestral percussion first; Art Blakey's "Blues March" the first beat he learned; "the first time I ever saw anyone play who really drove me insane was Ringo", then James Brown, Al Jackson and Benny Benjamin; Freddie Waits taught him privately after the Jazz Interactions classes; Steve Gadd, Harvey Mason and Dave Garibaldi "huge influences" in the late 1970s. "I can play the same beat a million different ways. It's about how it's tilted: What side of the quarter note I'm playing on? What do I want the hi-hat and kick to do?" Playing guitar and bass changed how he plays drums: he had been overplaying. The Groove Is Here DVD.

title: TT 418: "In Search of the Backbeat" (Ethan Iverson, Transitional Technology, July 2024)
notes: Notes to Iverson's piece on the Rolling Stones in The Nation, with Jordan's answer on his backbeat idols: "Al Jackson Jr. had one of the most recognizable, steady, precise and exacting backbeats. Benny Benjamin, Fred Below, Earl Palmer ... Clyde Stubblefield and Jabo Starks for James Brown."

title: The Rolling Stones Europa-Tour: Drummer Steve Jordan stellt sein Drumset vor (Bonedo, 2022)
notes: Though a Yamaha endorser, he plays Gretsch with the Stones: a black kit with a 24" bass drum and 13" and 14" toms, to come closer to Charlie Watts's sound, and a solid maple snare built for him; Paiste cymbals, and Charlie Watts's own Ufip china.
